question: Stress before a test makes recall slip. Which way of studying the day before protected memory against it?
answer: Testing oneself. Students learned material either by re-reading it or by taking practice tests; a day later, half gave a speech and did mental arithmetic in front of judges before recall. Stress cut recall among the re-readers but not among the self-testers. A memory pulled out many times has a well-worn path back.
move: Practise pulling knowledge out, not putting it in, before a high-stakes day.
ask: Before my next interview or exam, have I practised recalling the material, or only rereading it?
reference: Smith, Floerke & Thomas, Retrieval practice protects memory against acute stress, Science, 2016
